core_obligations: Reduction (2)=>(1): affine opens U,V; the Hom characterization of finite presentation (algebra-lemma-characterize-finite-presentation) becomes a Mor statement for T_i=Spec(A_i); the image-avoidance step Z_{i'}=g_{i'}^{-1}(X\U) nonempty for all i' leads, via lemma-limit-closed-nonempty, to a point of T missing U - contradiction.

Uniqueness (a) in (1)=>(3): the diagonal factors through the open W (union of U x_V U), scheme-theoretic argument via (g_i,g'_i); if Z_{i'} nonempty for all i', limit-closed-nonempty gives t in T outside W - contradiction; finite affine cover of quasi-compact T_i reduces to the affine case, closed via the algebra lemma plus fp of O_S(V)->O_X(U).

Existence (b): finite affine cover of T dominated by covers of X and S; lemma-descend-opens + lemma-limit-affine make W_j = lim W_{j,i}; the algebra lemma lifts each g|_{W_j} to some W_{j,i_j}; quasi-compactness of W_{j_1,i} \cap W_{j_2,i} (quasi-separated T_i) plus part (a) aligns the pieces at a common index; the lifted morphisms glue to T_{i'} -> X.
proof_roadmap: (2)=>(1): translate the Hom criterion into a Mor statement, lift images past the limit by the closed-nonempty contradiction.
(1)=>(3)(b): cover descent, generator lift, alignment and gluing.
difficulty_reason: Three-part equivalence proof: trivial (3)=>(2); (2)=>(1) via the algebra characterization of finite presentation, an affine-local reduction and the limit-closed-nonempty contradiction; (1)=>(3) with a uniqueness part (diagonal factors into the affine-diagonal open W, limit-closed-nonempty, affine reduction) and an existence part (finite affine covers, descend-opens, generator lift, gluing). Multi-lemma assembly with two genuinely different reduction arguments.

compared.difference: The sibling lemma handles objects/morphisms of finite presentation under base change; this proposition characterizes the lfp property itself through the Mor-vs-colimit identities (2)/(3). Different statements, and the sibling is used as a cited step inside this proof.
The companion lemma weakens (2)/(3) to surjectivity only, re-running the same argument; it is a different (weaker-hypothesis) statement delivered separately.
